conviction_note: Nothing about FY26 has been pre-released (the last statement is the 30 Mar 2026 interim's 'in line with expectations'), so the whole year, the second interim dividend and the first FY27 outlook are new on the day. That makes the move large: abs 9%, against a 7% base for new numbers, the name's 8.6% median and FY-results moves of -2.1/-10.3/-15.7, on a 1-analyst AIM stock with a ~5% bid-offer spread. The sign is close to balanced. Counterparty royalty bases are mixed to soft (Siemens Dx -5.5% comparable Apr-Jun, Roche Dx +3% CER), and a newsless +23% 20-day run-up raises the bar. Against that, the company has said it will hold the dividend from reserves, the CFO bought days before year-end, and the first IVD pTau217 clearance (Roche, 24 Aug) gives the neuro line a possible upside surprise. So p_up is 46 and the scaled number is -0.72. It sits near the findings' own sum of -0.2 because both rest on weak, offsetting evidence.

findings.finding: Bioventix's direct royalty counterparties were mixed to soft over its H2 (Jan-Jun 2026). Siemens Healthineers Diagnostics, which pays its troponin royalties, posted comparable revenue -5.5% in Apr-Jun 2026 on China rebasing and legacy-platform decline and guided another mid-single-digit decline. Roche Diagnostics grew +3% CER in H1 2026, with China pricing reform the drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue declines drove the FY24 (-10.3%) and FY25 (-15.7%) results days; flat-to-down core sales at the Mar 2026 interim were met with +6.9% after a -11% run-in
findings.why_not_priced: A one-analyst AIM name with no published FY26 revision after these prints. If the market had transmitted Siemens' -5.5% Diagnostics quarter, BVXP would not have rallied 23% in 20 sessions into the print with no RNS. Royalties are paid in arrears and reported only in the annual results, so this is the first release that can show it. It is still a proxy, because Bioventix's interim called troponin 'steady' and most revenue is vitamin D across many customers.
findings.independence: Roche H1 2026: Diagnostics +3% CER, Asia-Pacific down 'mainly due to the healthcare pricing reforms in China', https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2026-07-23

findings.finding: Roche's Elecsys pTau217 became the first FDA-cleared pTau217 blood test on a major automated IVD platform (24 Aug 2026; CE mark May 2026). Bioventix has said three of the leading IVD companies' RuO pT217 assays (it named Roche, Siemens, Abbott, Beckman, Quidel-Ortho and Mindray as the field) use a Bioventix SMA, without saying which. The FY results are the first company statement since the clearance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Mar 2026 interim's five-fold Tau royalty growth headline came with a +6.9% day, the only positive results day in six
findings.why_not_priced: Whether Bioventix is inside any cleared IVD assay is unknown to the market. There has been no RNS since 24 June, which leans against Bioventix being in Roche's assay: an IVD royalty stream would likely have been disclosed. If the market had priced a confirmed IVD royalty, the stock would trade well above the 1,750-2,000p range it has held since August. The rally since mid-September may already be leaning on this hope, so the range runs both ways.
findings.independence: Interim RNS on the RuO pT217 footprint: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/bioventix--bvxp/interim-results/9496897 ; Beckman's CE-marked pTau217 uses an ALZpath antibody, not Bioventix: https://allsci.com/news/approvals/beckman-coulters-ce-marked-p-tau217-blood-test-enables-scalable-alzheimers-screening-in-routine-labs/

findings.finding: The CFO bought 534 shares on market at 1,799p on 24 June 2026, six days before the financial year closed. The Chairman (1,000 shares at 1,848p) and the CEO with his wife (2,130 shares at 1,849p) bought in April.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured link on this name; directors also bought around the falling FY24/FY25 results
findings.why_not_priced: Small (about £9.6k) and four months old, and it was public. It is evidence only in that the CFO, with nearly all of the year's sales known, saw no reason to stay out. Royalty returns arrive in arrears, so his visibility was partial.

findings.finding: The board said in March that the business's resilience 'allow[s] the flexibility to use reserves to maintain our dividend at historic levels', and H1 cash was £5.3m after paying £4.18m of dividends. A second interim held at about 80p is the likely outcome, which removes the FY25-style dividend-cut tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY25: second interim cut from 87p to 80p, stock -15.7% on the day and -6.4% the next
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since it is a company statement; this lands inside what the company said. Around 7.5% yield names trade on the payout, so a hold mainly removes downside. Sized near 0 with a negative tail.

findings.finding: The stock rose from 1,500p (17 Sep) to 2,000p (22 Oct), +23% over 20 sessions, on rising volume and with no RNS since 24 June. It is the first results day in six reached on a positive run-up; the five before followed 20-day run-ups of -2% to -11%. FY results days have fallen three years running (-2.1%, -10.3%, -15.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself, and the baseline's lean (-1.15) already carries the run-up, so the finding is sized small for agreeing with the lean. What it adds is that a quiet 'in line' print now meets buyers who paid 30% more than in September for something the release may not deliver.
